Adenica (B58)

Region (English scoring-table division): East Cannor (Escann).

In one sentence: Raise the banner of Adean over the ruins of a knightly kingdom destroyed by the Greentide, rebuilding Cannor through warhorses, chivalric virtues and religious war.

Story: High｜Mission-tree length: Very long (54 direct B58 missions)｜Mission-tree update: the local mission file was modified on 2026-07-09 and supports v1.37.5.0｜Uniqueness: High｜Tedium: Medium-high (formation threshold and late war count)｜Early pressure: High (reclaiming Taranton from a predecessor)｜Expansion ability: Very high

The Destroyed Knightly Kingdom

Adenica is the current local name for Adenica (B58). Its texts remember a kingdom that was the centre of Adeanic faith and knightly tradition in western Escann before the Greentide; when the Greentide came, its knights fought until the kingdom fell. “The ancient country once existed” is not the same claim as “it can be selected directly in 1444.” The B58 country-history file predefines a monarchy, Adenner culture, the Regent Court religion and Taranton as capital, but current province history assigns Taranton to Spiderwretch (B46), and no B58 territory in 1444 was found. The country template cannot stand in for a starting-map fact.

The English offline Wiki lists Adenica as one of the major knightly-era kingdoms of Escann and dates its destruction to the 1424 Greentide. It does not establish a canonical modern restoration year or a unique restorer; the in-game B58 formation route is therefore a player-created future. The Halann historical map likewise confirms the ancient identity but has not audited B58 territory in 1444 or a restoration year as a historical node.

The normal playable entry is the formation decision in western Castanor: Regent Court faith, an Escanni culture or an Adventurer reform, Taranton, at least ten local provinces, administrative technology, independence and peace are the main gates; with the relevant DLC, choosing Adean as personal deity is also required. The decision changes the country to B58, moves the capital to Taranton, grants restoration claims and replaces the mission tree. It does not require one unique predecessor. There is also a special detour: Flying Hound (B43), after meeting hidden de-monsterisation and loyalty conditions, can call the same formation effect through a dedicated event and retain the special displayed name “Adean's Country”. That is an optional story route, not Adenica's standard starting point.

Virtues, Warhorses and the Court

The 54 missions are divided into five groups. The chivalric-virtue line turns justice, temperance, conviction, wisdom, responsibility and charity into individually completed goals; variables record progress and gradually turn the nobles' self-image into state institutions. “Demand Chivalric Oaths” can produce the Chivalric Nobility reform, while “Reorganise the Court” leads to the Mortal Court, which mirrors divine offices with mortal appointments. These mechanics connect cavalry, noble loyalty, religious alignment and governance; they are not merely a layer of flavour text. The 2021 dev diary identifies the virtues and the struggle over Adean's status as design priorities; current implementation remains governed by the local scripts.

The cavalry line moves from rebuilding the lance school, breeding warhorses and holding knightly tournaments toward a higher-grade army. The Grand Hunt allows choices of quarry and companions; the tournament can play safe, place bets or have the monarch challenge personally, with different costs and outcomes. “Purebred Breeding” even requires sacrificing cavalry units before improving the local herd. “The Knight's Weapon” requires treasury and mage support to forge a legendary lance and includes a waiting period; “Adean's Champion” later checks very high prestige and an accumulated war count. The late-game payoff is substantial, but it can feel like a checklist marathon: players who prefer speedruns may not enjoy repeated wars to close the route.

From Restoring East Cannor to a Cannorian Order

The geographic arc first secures Taranton and the old kingdom's plains, reclaims the roads toward Castanor, then expands through East Cannor and the wider Cannorian sphere. Here chivalry includes protecting the weak, charity and building courts and town halls, as well as the hierarchical duties of lords and subjects. The religious line aims to unite Regent Court loyalists and eventually challenge the political position of Corinites and Ravelians; “Propose to Corin” is a narrative contact point, not proof that every route reconciles. Later missions explicitly make the disappearance of other-faith countries an administrative objective, and some events can directly change the religion of orc and half-orc provinces. Adenica is both a restoration story and a state increasingly convinced that it has the right to define Cannor's order.

After forming B58, the player does not need to change to another Tag to see the full dedicated tree. A larger East Cannor formable remains an optional later detour and must not be back-projected as B58's inevitable end. The current scripts locate 54 direct B58 missions; the virtue lines can proceed in parallel, so the tree is not 54 strictly serial stages, and some late sections retain political and religious direction choices.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 84/100｜Autocracy 70/100｜Magic↔Artifice 55/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 27/100)｜Pluralism 28/100. The campaign prizes restoration across regions and knightly expeditions, with state power supported by monarchy, noble oaths and Regent Court organisation; magic appears through mage advisers and the legendary weapon but is not the main loop. Low pluralism reflects an explicit drive toward Regent Court and Adean religious unity, not a moral judgement based on religious enthusiasm alone.

The v2.1 values profile is Good (70/100) with a mixed trajectory. Protecting the weak, charity, courts and public administration have direct textual and mission support; the goal of forcibly removing other-faith polities and optional regional conversion limits personhood and restraint. War, monarchy, noble hierarchy and religious propagation are not scored by themselves; the specific coercive methods are what affect the assessment. This is for players who like traditional knightly fantasy, cavalry armies, restoration building, long virtue missions and religious politics. It is a poor fit if you do not want to meet a formation threshold first, dislike late accumulated-war goals or do not want a strong single-faith narrative. The 2026 player discussions focus on the hidden Flying Hound entry conditions and cavalry strength, which do not represent every normal formation route. Details and untested items are in the evidence page.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Adenica (B58) — Adenner Ideas

Set ID: B58_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B58
    }

Adenner Traditions

  • Missionary strength: +3% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.03).

  • Cavalry combat ability: +33% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.33).

1. Birthplace of Chivalry

The Kingdom of Adenica was the birthplace of the common ideals of "knights" and chivalry. When Adenica fell during the Greentide, that shining beacon of honour and chivalry was lost. With Adenica reforged again, we will rise to meet the ideals of our forefather and shine once more. With righteous hearts, our knights will reclaim their former glory as they ride against injustice.

  • Cavalry flanking ability: +100% (cavalry_flanking; raw value 1).

  • Cavalry to infantry ratio: +20% (cav_to_inf_ratio; raw value 0.2).

2. Sons of Adean

Adean is the first-born son of Castellos, and the god of honour, justice and chivalry. When our kingdom was founded, and now refounded, our people embraced these ideals in their entirety. To this end, every man, woman, and child holds this pledge in their hearts: "We are the spear of Adean and all he stands for. No matter what evil we face, we shall not falter."

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

3. The Corinite Heresy

There is no doubt in our minds that Corin deserved her ascent to godhood for her valiant sacrifice ending the Greentide. Yet this attempted usurpation of the Regent Court shows that perhaps it was truly Agrados reborn, not Corin ascendant, that has declared war upon the gods. The Corinites do not pledge themselves to Corin and her beliefs, but to Agrados. This vile heresy and desecration of both Corin's name and the Regent Court as a whole cannot be tolerated. We must be the spear of Adean once more.

  • Cost of enforcing religion through war: -50% (enforce_religion_cost; raw value -0.5).

4. Born to Fight

When Castanor fell, Adenica fought for its sovereignty against the other successor states. It fought to the last as the Greentide brought ruin to Escann. Even when struck down, its spirit continued to fight. And, through fire, blood and steel, Adenica was reforged. Adenners have never feared fighting for what was right and they are ready and willing to continue that fight once more.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

5. Land of Honor

In Adenica, we pride ourselves on our high standards of honourable conduct. It is a core element of our culture and society, second only to our faith. This high level of honour and respect has led to a vastly lower level of corruption, blackmail and abuse of power within our bureaucracy.

  • Yearly corruption: -0.1 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.10).

6. Knight-Kings of Adenica

To rule in Adenica, you must prove yourself worthy of rule. To do this, one must obtain knighthood before ascending to the throne. This has been a long standing tradition within our kingdom, and has proven profoundly useful. Our Knight-Kings are known throughout the world for their chivalrous and honourable conduct, and are role models to many rulers and heir-apparents. This reputation has left us in good standing within the global community.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

7. Between the Titans

Our proximity to both the Empire of Anbennar and the reborn realms of Escann have provided us a unique opportunity. We are able to draw on the regulations and innovations of the Western Cannorians, and the military expertise from the Escanni realms. We can leverage this advantage to stay head of the curve, and ensure our ability to protect those in need.

  • Global institution spread: +20% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.2).

Adenner Ambitions

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

Flying Hound (B43) — Flying Hound Ideas

Set ID: B43_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B43
    }

Flying Hound Traditions

  • Looting speed: +50% (loot_amount; raw value 0.5).

  • Military advisor cost: -25% (mil_advisor_cost; raw value -0.25).

1. Bred for the Dismounted

Even though our clan is very young, its history can be traced back to the early days of the Greentide. When orcs invaded, they dragged their goblin slaves out with them from the Serpentspine. Many of these goblins came riding on the backs of giant spiders. These giant spider riders were a fearsome force; however, they had a major downside. Giant spiders are not native to Escann, so when a goblin lost their mount in battle, it was extremely expensive, if possible at all, to get a replacement. What wasn’t rare to find in Escann were dogs; plenty of stray dogs roamed the now war-ravaged land. Dismounted riders soon began using dogs as replacements, and almost immediately after that, they began breeding them to improve speed and riding capability. As the cohesion of the Greentide started to collapse, many of these now-free dog riders came together and formed the Flying Hound clan.

  • Cavalry recruitment cost: -20% (cavalry_cost; raw value -0.20).

2. Goblins Sneaky Tactics

We goblins were nothing but fodder to the Dookanson, used as flimsy meat shields. And while we were slaughtered by adventurer firearms, the orcs mindlessly charged after the first barrage, running over every dying goblin and bringing them to an agonising end.

Now that we are free, this will no longer be. We will fight as we learned in the darkness of the caverns, cleverly hiding and attacking with poisoned arrows, ambushing enemy leaders and bleeding their armies. This is the way of goblin warfare, and it is the way we will forever follow as long as we are free.

  • shock_damage_received: -10% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.10).

3. Rabid Campaigns

When news of the Dookanson's death spread, nearly every goblin was ecstatic, but left feeling very uncertain about the future. Not Elgek, though. When word reached his ears, it is said you could just tell he saw opportunity from the look that was shining forth from his eyes and his big grin. Immediately Elgek sounded a rallying cry which amassed many goblins to his side, especially amongst dog riders who eventually dubbed him clanboss of the Flying Hound clan. Unfortunately, Elgek did not turn out to be the great military mind of our time. He ended up blindly rushing us into wars and picking fights wherever he could, damn the consequences. Luckily, we did soon learn that Elgek had a great knack for diplomacy. When enraged foreign diplomats came barging in and demanding answers for his actions, Elgek always knew exactly what to say and how to steer the conversation in his favor. It was hard to stay mad at such a charismatic personality after having a chat with him, and he managed to get the clan out of facing the worst possible consequences many times. Since his passing, the clan has tried to adopt his style of diplomacy going forward.

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -10% (ae_impact; raw value -0.1).

4. Life Under The Blue Sky

Though still a hostile place with our former captors and adventurers still lurking, Escann is a much more pleasant place to live than the Serpentspine, with its lush forests and serene lakes. Here, we need not fight over any source of food or water for there is plenty for all.

With this bounty has come changes among the clans. The ancient traditions celebrated in the darkness of the caves are now festivals in the sunlight and under the shadow of ancient ruined temples consecrated to the many gods of mankind. In this beautiful place, we gblins can create something better than our ancient homeland. Perhaps we found a home at last.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

5. Looting For Knowledge

Escann is not only rich in food and resources, but also knowledge. Among the old human ruins are books, scrolls and all manner of written stuffs that survived the desolation brought by the Dookanson. All as valuable as any other loot.

However, these texts are written in a language unlike the crude tongue of the Dwarves we came to grudgingly learn. If we are to make use of this treasure we must decipher this language. Fortunately, we goblins are equally cunning and intelligent. To learn this "common" script, we will capture those adventurers who can and force them to teach us the language of humanity, and learn from the knowledge left by those who inhabited these beautiful lands before us

  • Technology cost: -2.5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.025).

  • Idea cost: -5% (idea_cost; raw value -0.05).

6. The Naegub

With the progressive modernisation of the clans, a new social class is emerging, created by those goblins who are considered within the clan to be the most astute and have the best manners, as well as having managed to adapt more quickly to the language of humanity than their congeners. They are the Naegub.

Ranging from merchants to negotiators and even diplomats, they act as the link between the clan and the realms of the other civilised races. They are involved in every transaction and negotiation, be they commercial or political, always wringing the most they can for the clan (and themselves). As such, it is a role of great power. Something that garners immense respect, and envy, within the clan.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

7. Days of the Speed Demons

Towards the later years of the Greentide, our sense of identity as a people and the culture of our clan truly began to develop. A wave of fanaticism swept across our clan, which took the art of riding beyond the battlefield and into the hands of the average goblin. No longer was a mount restricted to the rich goblin; instead, all could afford to buy a riding dog, and that they did. Mounted dog races became the most popular and common sport in our lands. Many goblin clothiers began expanding their work to include fashion for dog mounts. One could not go anywhere within our domain and not see a goblin without his ride; the two were inseparable! Joined at the hip! To be a goblin of the Flying Hound clan was to be a goblin and your dog mount. This came full circle, as it was clear that most goblins within our society wouldn't do anything without a mount, and most recruits refused to even go into battle while on foot.

  • Cavalry to infantry ratio: +25% (cav_to_inf_ratio; raw value 0.25).

  • Movement speed: +10% (movement_speed; raw value 0.1).

Flying Hound Ambition

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).
